=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:981,1109-1147,1200-1207 (minimax also cites cmd_state_update around line 1240) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: render_model_input() spends the byte budget on "## Flagged items" before "## New blocked items", so new blocked items can be marked `omitted`. classify() has already stored their fingerprint with diagnosed_run=run_id, and state_update() commits state-next.json unchanged, so these items are recorded as diagnosed even though the model never saw them.
  WHY: On the next run the fingerprint matches, so the item counts as known and never gets a root cause or AUD plan (violates G4). The checker also drops omitted entries from required refs. Severities differ: minimax=BLOCKER, sonnet/luna/glm=MAJOR, gemini gave none; the highest is used.
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:754-761,776,823-830,947-949 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: _detail_priority() gives priority 3 to an old issue reopened in the window that has no `ai:` label and is not an open PR. collect() therefore never fetches its details, reopened_since(None) returns False, and classify() skips the item.
  WHY: This is exactly the reopened-item case the new gate was meant to catch. The `reopened` signal and tier-1 classification are lost and Coverage under-counts. The regression test only covers the ai:-labelled path (priority 1). Severity: sonnet/minimax/luna/glm=MAJOR, gemini gave none.
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:157,433-437,942-943,984-988 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: load_settings() accepts ISSUE_PR_AUDIT_MAX_OPEN_PAGES=0, and list_open() then returns ([], False) without reading anything. classify() treats this as a full snapshot, adds the repo to full_snapshot_displays, and drops its tracked blocked entries from next_state.
  WHY: Every known blocked entry is erased from the committed state, including its `since`, so the items look new again once the value is restored. Severities differ: sonnet=NIT, minimax/luna/glm=MAJOR, gemini gave none; the highest is used.
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:984-988 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The carry-over condition `key.rsplit("#", 1)[0] not in full_snapshot_displays` keeps blocked entries forever for repositories that are no longer audited: archived, excluded, access lost, cut by the repo cap, or switched between redacted and plain display.
  WHY: analysis/issue_pr_audit_state.json grows without bound with stale entries that no run can clear, and they ship in every audit PR diff. Severity: NIT from all who stated one (gemini gave none).
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:942-943,986-988,1202-1206 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The carry-over compares old blocked-state keys with the current display name. If private-repository redaction is turned off for one run and then back on, the old key holds the plain repository name while the current set holds `private:<hash>`, so the plain-name key is copied into the next state.
  WHY: The delivery step commits that state file, which exposes the private repository name and issue number on a public host even though redaction is enabled.
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:963-981,984-988,1006 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When an open snapshot is truncated or a repo read fails, classify() carries known blocked entries into next_state but never adds them to the `blocked` list, so digest["blocked"] leaves them out.
  WHY: The report's Blocked Items section and the Telegram message (render_telegram reads digest["blocked"]) miss long-blocked items, which violates G7.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:render_model_input() lines 1109-1135 (the section order puts "## Flagged items" before "## New blocked items", and line 1132 sets entry["omitted"] = True); classify() line 981 (writes next_state["blocked"][state_key] with the fingerprint and diagnosed_run=run_id); state_update() lines 1200-1207 (copies next_state unchanged) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The whole-entry byte cap can leave out new blocked items, which are marked omitted, and the checker (scripts/check_issue_pr_audit_report.py required_refs, lines 76-79) no longer requires them. classify has already written their fingerprint into state-next.json, and state_update commits it as is.
  WHY: 80 deep items (3,000-char body plus five 2,000-char comments each) can pass the 600,000-byte budget. An unseen new blocked item is then committed with its fingerprint, counts as known (new=False) next run, and never gets a root cause or AUD plan. Fix: blank the stored fingerprint for new+omitted entries, or render "New blocked items" first.
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:_detail_priority() lines 754-761; the `if priority < 3` filter at line 829; the classify() gate `if not in_window(item, cursor) and not reopened_since(detail, cursor): continue` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A reopened issue with no ai: label that is not an open PR gets priority 3 and its details are never fetched, so reopened_since() returns False and classify skips it.
  WHY: The item gets no tier-1 classification, no `reopened` signal, and is missing from the Coverage count. The regression test only covers the ai:-labelled path (priority 1).
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:load_settings() line 157 (max_open_pages allows 0); list_open() line 433 (returns [], False when max_open_pages == 0); classify() lines 942-943 and 987 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: With ISSUE_PR_AUDIT_MAX_OPEN_PAGES=0, list_open reports truncated=False, so the repo lands in full_snapshot_displays and its known blocked entries are not carried over.
  WHY: Every tracked blocked entry, including `since`, is cleared from committed state, and the items count as new with reset ages once the value is restored.
- scripts/issue_pr_audit.py:classify() lines 984-988 (`key.rsplit("#", 1)[0] not in full_snapshot_displays`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Blocked entries for repositories that are no longer audited (archived, excluded, access lost, repo cap, redacted/plain switch) are kept forever.
  WHY: analysis/issue_pr_audit_state.json keeps stale blocked entries indefinitely. They never reach the digest or Telegram.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh gains APPLY_ANALYSIS_DOC_GLOB_EXTRA (default a
